def: to strip off, i.e. (partially) scrape; by implication, to segregate (as an angle)

occurrences.text: And he shall cause the house to be scraped within round about, and they shall pour out the dust that they scrape off without the city into an unclean place:
In the four corners of the court there were courts joined of forty cubits long and thirty broad: these four corners were of one measure.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
